description: Hello, we are a group of third-year compsci students, from the Philippines' national engineering university, ready to build! We're a team looking forward to learning new tech, surviving the sleepless hackathon grind with generous amounts of coffee, and playing lots of Roblox :)
summary:
Project ARES (Astronaut Resistance & Exercise System) is an offline-first, AI-driven fitness coach designed to combat musculoskeletal degradation and psychological burnout during long-duration spaceflight. Because deep-space communication delays prevent real-time Earth supervision, ARES functions as an autonomous, on-board personal trainer.

The experience begins with a pre-flight onboarding module where astronauts input baseline health and physical metrics. The system's AI core then generates a personalized, dynamically adjusting workout regimen. Using standard cabin cameras and in-browser 33-point computer vision, ARES monitors joint angles, counts reps, and corrects lifting form in real time without requiring wearable sensors or active Earth connectivity.

To fight the monotony of multi-year confinement, ARES transforms daily workout volume into gamified planetary milestones, such as traversing the Valles Marineris. By automatically logging kinematic telemetry locally and batch-syncing with flight surgeons once signal is re-established, ARES safeguards crew health in zero-gravity while offering scalable applications for remote terrestrial physical therapy.
details:
PROJECT ARES operates as a closed-loop biomechanical tracking system that begins with a baseline calibration phase. Astronauts input their mass, bone density metrics, and current one-rep max, allowing the system’s routing algorithm to generate a phased, adaptive workout calendar tailored to their specific mission duration. During the actual workout, the architecture relies entirely on edge computing to overcome the 24-minute communication latency of deep space. By capturing the video feed from existing cabin cameras and processing it through an in-browser machine learning model built with Google MediaPipe Pose, the system isolates 33 skeletal landmarks in 3D space at over 30 frames per second. As the astronaut moves, the application continuously calculates geometric joint angles, instantly triggering auditory and visual form-correction alerts via a lightweight React and Vite-powered interface if a movement deviates from a safe range of motion.

Because this computer vision pipeline runs locally without sending a single byte of data back to Earth, it enables strict adherence to heavy resistance training protocols without the injury risks associated with unmonitored lifting. Caching this kinematic data via Supabase and IndexedDB offloads the mental burden of manually counting reps and logging sets, allowing astronauts to focus entirely on physical exertion. This frictionless telemetry directly addresses the severe constraints of Mars-bound missions, preserving vital bone mineral density and muscle mass while operating seamlessly even during complete communication blackouts.

Our team’s most creative engineering decision was completely avoiding the use of IoT wearables or specialized tracking suits, which add payload weight, require charging, and are prone to hardware failure in high-radiation environments. By utilizing in-browser AI and standard RGB webcams, we engineered a zero-latency software solution with absolutely no physical footprint. To further counter the psychological isolation and motivational burnout of multi-year confinement, we transformed dry medical telemetry into an interactive experience. Mapping a crew's cumulative lifted tonnage and exercise volume to virtual planetary milestones, such as hiking Olympus Mons, turns a mandatory medical protocol into an engaging, crew-wide mission achievement.

Beyond space exploration, this exact architecture possesses a highly scalable terrestrial impact. By removing the financial and technical barriers of specialized tracking sensors, ARES can democratize physical therapy and at-home fitness on Earth. It empowers patients in remote or underserved areas to receive high-level, real-time biomechanical coaching using nothing more than a standard laptop or smartphone camera.
